terra is a transitive dependency via: leaflet → raster → terra
Affected users cannot deploy any app using leaflet on shinyapps.io.

or provide a pre-built binary of terra for GDAL 3.4.1.

title: Add ability to mark packages as unsupported
description:
I have had to remove at least three or four packages from this repo in total because they were removed from CRAN and so the CI pipeline would be unable to find the package. These packages are still available in the CRAN archive and a user or a manifest could potentially still install an old version of them, but when we remove the install script, we still break the application.

I think a more gentle solution that could benefit users who have pinned old dependencies is to mark certain packages as unsupported, causing CI to skip them but still allowing them to keep doing what they always did in case a user managed to install an archived version of the package.

```
library(shiny)
library(magick)

ui <- fluidPage(
   
   # Application title
   titlePanel("Magick Density"),
   
   # Sidebar with a slider input for density
   sidebarLayout(
      sidebarPanel(
         sliderInput("density",
                     "Density:",
                     min = 150,
                     max = 2000,
                     value = 1200)
      ),
      
      # Show image as png
      mainPanel(
         imageOutput("ximage")
      )
   )
)

# Define server logic
server <- function(input, output) {
   
   output$ximage <- renderImage({
      image <-  image_convert(image_read(path="https://github.com/jhcreed/bustedMagick/raw/master/pdf/DAGimageDoc.pdf", 
                                         density = paste0(input$density,"x",input$density)),
                              "png")
      tmpfile <- image %>%
         image_write(path=paste0(getwd(),"/image.png"),
                     format = 'png')
      
      list(src = tmpfile)
   })
}

# Run the application 
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

title: ssh key menu
description:
This has been discusses already a bit in 
* #20 - providing ssh tunneling with ssh pass,
* [Remote MySQL database with SSH Tunnel](https://groups.google.com/d/msg/shinyapps-users/J7i_wcU6_uA/r6-wZ6lHuJoJ) - ssh tunneling with keys, but in a way which needs to add your keys inside your app code somehow, which doesn't make any sense.

**Having a more generic solution makes more sense to me: can shinyapps.io not provide `ssh keys` item in the dashboard, on which (private) keys can be uploaded?**

 This is not an uncommon thing to do in hosted services, and really helpful in many ways. It would mean one can control the keys/security (host related) separated from the app itself. Shinyapp.io could place the key in the usual `.ssh` directory of the user, so having a command like `ssh -L <port>:localhost:<port> shinyapp@<host> -nNT` (ran from R) would do (if the keys are generated for a user 'shinyapp'). Or one might even think of running such a command from the dashboard as well (you only need to know port and host to connect to, so inside each `ssh key` item, on might even supply a port, host and start/stop button).

title: Add support for sshpass
description:
I would like to use ssh tunnel to then access mysql database, and collect and pass on the password via a passwordInput field. This would require having sshpass installed on the instances (http://sourceforge.net/projects/sshpass/)

The current proposed method
(https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/shinyapps-users/J7i_wcU6_uA)
 involves placing the private ssh key for shinyapps in with the application files. I would like an alternative where you could collect the ssh password (or mysql password) via a passwordInput field and pass it on to the ssh or sql connection parameters.

Then the method would look something like this (adapted from suggestion in shinyapps group:

system(paste0("sshpass -p '",input$remotesyspassword,"' ssh -f -L 3306:localhost:3306 username@remotsystemhostname sleep 20")).

The advantage of this method is that you are not storing a private key remotely, and rely on the user knowing/entering the password just as they would in an interactive ssh session.

title: Allow to deploy with CRAN packages installed with r-cran on Debian/Ubuntu
description:
On Debian/Ubuntu system, CRAN packages can be installed in the usual way from within R, or through the .deb package system installing r-cran-\* packages, thanks among others to the ppa of Michael rutter: https://launchpad.net/%7Emarutter/+archive/ubuntu/c2d4u  

This results in virtually the same package installed, but unfortunately, is currently not allowed when deploying shinyapps, that will return an error message: 
     _The package was installed locally from source_

It would be great if having installed CRAN packages through this system would not prevent deploying the app, and if validateRepository() had a mechanism to detect packages installed with the r-cran-\* system, and tolerate them (maybe under some conditions, such as same version, etc...).   

Not this is distinct, though related, to the issue 4 (https://github.com/rstudio/shinyapps-package-dependencies/issues/4), suggesting to use internally the r-cran-\* system.

title: automatically install the dependencies using the c2d4u PPA
description:
It seems we have been trying to install the dependencies of R packages on a case by case basis, and actually this problem has been solved by Michael Rutter long time ago: https://launchpad.net/~marutter/+archive/ubuntu/c2d4u

```
sudo apt-get install -y software-properties-common
sudo add-apt-repository -y ppa:marutter/c2d4u
```

Then if you want to install the binary package **foo**, you can `sudo apt-get install r-cran-foo`. If you want to install its build dependencies so that you can install the source package, you can `sudo apt-get build-dep r-cran-foo`. There might be a few packages that still need our manual inspection to figure out their dependencies, but this should be very rare.

A further thought is, how about just let users install whatever they want? Just like Travis CI. Then we will not have to worries about these dependencies. Of course, we may need to add some constraints (such as memory/disk space).

title: rJava install script missing -y flag on apt-get, breaks builds when base image has pending upgrades
description:
## Summary

`packages/rJava/install` calls `apt-get install bzip2 libbz2-dev` without the `-y` flag. When the jammy base image has pending upgrades for these packages, `apt` prompts for confirmation. With no stdin in the build environment, the prompt aborts, and `set -e` fails the entire image build.

## Current script

```
#!/bin/bash
set -x
set -e

apt-get update -qq
apt-get install bzip2 libbz2-dev
```

## Expected

```
apt-get install -y bzip2 libbz2-dev
```

## Impact

This blocks deployment for any application with an rJava dependency (including transitive, e.g. via the `xlsx` package). The bug is latent: it only triggers when the base image's `bzip2`/`libbz2-dev` packages are behind and `apt` has changes to apply. Build logs show `3 upgraded and 146 not upgraded`, indicating the jammy base has fallen behind.

For contrast, `packages/fs/install` in the same repo correctly passes `-y`:
```
apt-get install -y libuv1-dev
```

## Audit

Checked all 52 install scripts in the repo that call `apt-get install`. **`packages/rJava/install` is the only one missing `-y`.**

## Suggested fix

Add `-y` to the `apt-get install` call in `packages/rJava/install`, or set `DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive` for the script.

## Reported via

Zendesk support ticket from a customer whose production shinyapps.io app cannot be redeployed due to this bug.
